https://www.dw.com/en/indonesia-neutrali.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IxUm China carries out frequent military drills around Taiwan [FILE: December 2025] Image: Taiwan Coast Guard/AFP Advertisement On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill. Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy. Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022. Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training." China's gray zone warfare in the Pacific To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance. "It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said. Indonesia dragged into sensitive geopolitics However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan . "Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said. Kabinawa added that passing exercises were among the lowest-level naval activities yet used by China to justify its intimidation of Taiwan. "Indonesia must also exercise caution in this regard," she said, adding that Jakarta should "not to be too naive," to assume that its participation in a "regular exercise" with China would not cause concern in Taiwan. Jakarta's nonaligned foreign policy in focus Indonesia has stood by its "free and active" foreign policy for over half a century, distinguishing itself from neighboring countries that align with China or the US. However, both Beijing and Washington want the world's largest island nation to be part of their Asia-Pacific strategy . Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto met with Elbridge Colby, a US undersecretary of defense, in Jakarta on the same day as the controversial passing exercise with China. While Prabowo also visits Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, Jakarta has shown its willingness to accept US requests for blanket overflights, which allows US military aircraft access to Indonesian airspace. Chong Ja Ian, an associate professor of political science at the National University of Singapore, told DW that Indonesia's neutral stance is a product of pressure from superpowers. "The principle of free and active foreign policy wouldn't change much, but we'll wait and see how Jakarta operates it," he said. How China's rise is shaping Trump's strategy in Asia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Researcher Kabinawa said the current Indonesian administration lacks clear guidelines for interpreting its foreign policy amid intensifying geopolitical tension, especially across the Taiwan Strait. However, she added that it would be unlikely for Indonesia to be involved in any Chinese invasion scenario of Taiwan. "I would always remind everyone that there are 350,000 Indonesian citizens in Taiwan who need to be protected or maybe evacuated if that hypothetical scenario happens," she said. According to Taiwan's official data, Indonesians are the largest group of foreign residents in the country. "So I don't think Indonesia would get involved in being a combatant, but rather involved in trying to evacuate their citizens,” Kabinawa said. "That would risk the political and economic stability of the country [Indonesia] itself.” Iryanda Mardanuz in Jakarta contributed to this article. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/17/nyil.text: Menü Kereső Nyílt pályázaton keresnek új vezetőt a Hungary Helps Ügynökség élére Belföld Dévai László Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Velkey György László, a Külgazdasági és Külügyminisztérium parlamenti államtitkára a Facebook-oldalán jelentette be , hogy új vezetőt keresnek a Hungary Helps Ügynökség élére. A pozícióra nyílt pályázatot írnak ki. Velkey szerint a kormány továbbra is segítséget akar nyújtani a világ válságban lévő, szegénységgel, természeti katasztrófákkal vagy más problémákkal küzdő közösségeinek. Hozzátette ugyanakkor, hogy a Hungary Helps Ügynökségnek a jövőben „tisztán, átláthatóan és felelősen” kell működnie. A Hungary Helps Ügynökség a magyar kormány humanitárius és fejlesztési programjainak végrehajtásában vesz részt, többek között válságövezetekben és rászoruló közösségek támogatásában. A pályázati kiírás szerint az új vezérigazgató várhatóan október 15-én kezdi meg a munkát, határozatlan idejű munkaviszonyban. A jelentkezőktől legalább egyetemi vagy mesterfokozatú diplomát, tárgyalóképes angolt, legalább tíz év releváns szakmai gyakorlatot és ezen belül legalább öt év vezetői tapasztalatot várnak el. Előnyt jelent többek között a humanitárius vagy segélyezési programokban, illetve állami, nonprofit vagy civil szervezetek vezetésében szerzett tapasztalat, valamint további nyelvek ismerete. A munkakör betöltéséhez érvényes nemzetbiztonsági szakvélemény is szükséges, a pályázatokat szeptember 15-ig lehet benyújtani. A Hungary Helps tevékenységéhez kapcsolódik a magyar kormány csádi szerepvállalása is, aminek keretében magyar iroda is működik az afrikai országban. Photograph: BBC View image in fullscreen Sisters Hema Sunil Amin, left, and Hemangini Jitendra Patel are unaccounted for after the flooding in Nepal. Photograph: BBC Nepal-Tibet flood disaster Daughter traces mother and aunt’s last known location in Nepal through TikTok video Tulshi Patel says mother Hemangini Jitendra Patel and aunt Hema Sunil Amin were last seen at Friendship Bridge on Nepal-China border Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates Sammy Gecsoyler Sat 29 Aug 2026 13.01 EDT Last modified on Sat 29 Aug 2026 13.49 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The daughter of a woman missing in Nepal has told how she traced her mother’s location through a TikTok video posted hours before the devastating flash flood hit. The catastrophic flash floods that hit Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday , thundering down valleys and sweeping away entire villages, have killed at least 675 people, while more than 3,000 remain missing . Among the missing are 33 British nationals, including a 13-year-old, NHS workers and a priest. A team from the UK will arrive in the Nepali capital, Kathmandu, on Saturday. Tulshi Patel’s mother, Hemangini Jitendra Patel, and her aunt, Hema Sunil Amin, set off on a pilgrimage in which they had planned to travel into Tibet , but the pair have not been contactable since the flash floods hit. In an interview with LBC’s Matt Frei, Patel said the two women had been talking about the trip since the start of the year and the journey had been “on their bucket list”. She said she had last spoken to her mother and aunt on Monday, had received a photo of them on Tuesday, and their last known location had come from a GPS signal from the tour group at a place called Friendship Bridge at the Nepal-China border. View image in fullscreen The Chinese immigration centre on the Tibet border. The green Friendship Bridge which crosses the river between Tibet and Nepal was swept away in the floods. Photograph: Armand Terruli/Guardian Community Patel, a pharmacist from Milton Keynes, said: “We did our own deep-dive research and we found a TikTok video that verified and showed my mum and auntie and three other people from the tour at the border waiting to cross, I guess, that the local Nepali tour guide had made.” Of the video, Patel said: “It was Wednesday morning, just before 6am, Nepal time. “They were supposed to have crossed the border on Tuesday, but I guess due to weather conditions, or whichever it was, they got delayed and unfortunately crossed over on Wednesday.” The flood is believed to have occurred after a magnitude 5.2 seismic event near the border between Nepal and China on Wednesday at 8.37am local time, according to the US Geological Survey. Patel said her mother and aunt had been in good health and had prepared well for the trip. “They’d gone on walks regularly, they were looking forward to it. This is all they wanted,” she said. “Their positive viewpoints, health, mental health was great and they were very strong and positive about everything. “This was something that they were both looking forward to. They’d been talking about this from the beginning of the year. It was something that was on their bucket list that they really wanted to do.” Neetu Goyal Tiwari. Photograph: Facebook Patel said she had messaged the two women “in the hopes that maybe we’ll see a tick to say they’ve seen it or read it” and had attempted to contact the tour guide. “We’ve messaged the tour guide in case he has a signal because he’ll have a local Sim as well. “Every day we’re calling via WhatsApp … We’ve not given up, but, from our end, all we can do is research, but we just need kind of eyes and ears there from our side to basically get them out. Get all of them out and safe.” Patel said the family had considered travelling to Nepal to join search efforts but had decided against this as they did not know how close they could get to the region in order to help. View image in fullscreen Leena Bector. Photograph: Facebook Some of those missing were visiting Kailash Mansarovar, a high-altitude site in ‌Tibet revered by Hindus and Buddhists. Neetu Goyal Tiwari, 51, was on her “dream” trip to complete a pilgrimage when the flash floods hit. The family have been desperately phoning contacts in Nepal in an attempt to find her, though they increasingly believe her to still be in China. As many of the family members are based in India, it is difficult for them to obtain visas to search for her. Her brother, Naresh Goyal, said Neetu’s husband and daughter remained in the UK for now. “We’re not sure what the next second holds and what we should do from our end, because we’re trying to reach everyone we can,” he said. “She was a very fun-loving woman [and] really had a great heart. I really hope she comes back soon.” Other families of those missing have travelled to the affected region from the UK. Leena Bector, 53, from Slough, was among 27 travellers who are unaccounted for. Her husband, Bhupesh Bector, told the Times he was booking the next flight to Kathmandu after the Home Office had failed to confirm whether Leena was on its missing persons list. He said: “Even if they find her today or tomorrow, I need to be there. She must be in trauma.” Explore more on these topics Nepal-Tibet flood disaster Nepal Tibet South and central Asia Natural disasters news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development
